monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by reduced average HR, increased Z1/Z2 time, and improved aerobic efficiency — though at the cost of pace and training effect intensity compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 time rose from 55% to 86%, while Z3–Z5 dropped from 45% to 13%, indicating a conscious, sustained aerobic base-building phase.

goal_tracker.message: You need 11.8 more km across 4 remaining sessions — averaging 2.95 km/session — to match last month’s volume. Given your recent long run (9.5 km) and current weekly rhythm, adding two 5–6 km Zone 2 runs in the next 10 days would close this gap efficiently.

insights.title: Efficiency dip despite cadence gain
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.09 m/km per spm, even as cadence rose +1 spm — suggesting stride length (down from avg 77.3 cm in Apr to 70.2 cm in May’s recent runs) and/or ground contact time (up from ~310 ms avg in Apr to 318 ms in May) are limiting force application efficiency.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and VO2 work
insights.body: Zero time spent in Z4 or Z5 this month (vs 19% last month), and Z3 dropped from 26% to 13% — meaning no structured efforts above ~85% HRmax, which may delay VO2 max progression despite recent VO2 readings rising from 36.0 to 37.0.

insights.title: Ground contact time increased under fatigue
insights.body: Ground contact time averaged 351 ms during the 9.5 km run (May 6) — 41 ms higher than your May avg (310 ms) and 30+ ms above April’s typical range — indicating form breakdown late in long efforts, likely contributing to vertical oscillation increase (+0.6 cm vs Apr avg).

insights.title: Low HR and high Z1 time signal intentional recovery focus
insights.body: Avg HR dropped 9 bpm and Z1 time rose to 39% (from 23%), aligning with reduced pace and aerobic TE — consistent with an active recovery or base-building intent, especially given the 9.5 km long run at only 131 bpm (well below Z2 ceiling).

recommendations.action: Do a 4 km Zone 2 run tomorrow (HR 128–135 bpm) with cadence ≥145 spm and stride length target ≥72 cm (use real-time Garmin metrics)
recommendations.reason: Your recent runs show cadence can hit 149–150 spm but stride length drops below 72 cm when pace slows — this session reinforces neuromuscular coordination at low HR without fatigue.

recommendations.action: Insert one 6-minute Z3 interval (HR 145–152 bpm) embedded in a 7 km total Zone 2 run on May 20 — e.g., 2 km warm-up, 6 min @ Z3, 3 km cool-down
recommendations.reason: You’ve done zero Z3+ work this month, and last month’s Z3 time (26%) correlated with your fastest pace (428 sec/km); reintroducing brief, controlled threshold stimulus will support aerobic power without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: After your next long run (>8 km), perform 3 × 1-min barefoot strides on grass focusing on light ground contact (<280 ms) and minimal vertical oscillation (<6.5 cm)
recommendations.reason: Your longest run showed elevated ground contact (351 ms) and vertical oscillation (7.1 cm); these strides reinforce springy mechanics post-fatigue, directly targeting form decay observed in May 6 data.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthening the link between low-heart-rate effort, efficient stride mechanics, and controlled neuromuscular output — not just logging volume, but refining how you move at easy intensities.
suggested_sessions: 4 km Zone 2 run with cadence/stride-length targets
7 km mixed run with 6-min Z3 segment
